extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals and marketers planning/distributing press releases and launch communications in 2024
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for creating and distributing press releases in 2024, emphasizing modern channels (LinkedIn, podcasts, social), founder visibility, and which outlets still read traditional releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive news (not vanity announcement)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release must contain genuine news or meaningful updates — vanity, promotional-only announcements are not sufficient. This remains a core requirement ('What hasn't changed' and in the 'Quality Rubric'). Aim for real developments, data, milestones, or materials that reporters and aggregators can use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributed across modern channels
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't rely solely on the wire: distribute on modern platforms (LinkedIn newsletter/posts, Substack, social carousels, podcasts, TikTok/Reels) to reach target audiences. The piece should be tailored for each channel rather than copy-pasted boilerplate.

rubrics_metrics.name: LinkedIn-first distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute to LinkedIn FIRST (newsletter and posts)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For B2B and many business announcements, prioritize LinkedIn distribution (both newsletter and feed posts) as the primary channel. The article notes LinkedIn newsletter has taken the role of traditional press releases for B2B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Podcast co-launch pairing
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-launch with podcast appearance same day
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate launch timing with a podcast appearance to amplify reach and provide long-form context. 'Co-launch with podcast appearance same day' is recommended as a best practice for 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder TikTok/Reel on launch day
rubrics_metrics.description: Make founder do TikTok/Reel on launch day
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For consumer- and social-native audiences, have the founder post a TikTok/Reel on launch day. The memo notes TikTok-first product launches often skip press entirely — founder-led short-form video is a primary distribution channel.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEO/Founder visible voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the founder/CEO is a visible communicator for the announcement—via social posts, newsletter, or interview. 'Founder mode' announcements increasingly originate from the CEO's social channels rather than through traditional PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use first-person 'I' voice in CEO blog post
rubrics_metrics.description: Use first-person "I" voice in CEO blog post
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the CEO posts a blog/letter (e.g., on Substack), use a first-person 'I' voice to make the communication feel authentic and direct; this is a specific recommended tactic in 2024 best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia and visual assets for social-native consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia for social-native consumption / Visual assets needed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include photos, short videos, carousels, or other visual assets optimized for social platforms. The page emphasizes that visual assets remain necessary and that releases should be consumable in social-native formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save the wire for institutional credibility, not reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Wire for SEO credibility, not reach
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use wire distribution primarily for institutional/archival/SEO credibility rather than expecting it to drive broad reach. The piece notes wire services are now owned by financial-data companies and that the wire's role has shifted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo etiquette
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traditional embargo rules still apply: coordinate timelines and respect embargoes with journalists and partners. Embargos remain an unchanged expectation for certain kinds of news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spokesperson availability requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a spokesperson is available for interviews and verification at launch. The page lists spokesperson availability as a continued requirement — reporters expect access to on-the-record sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of facts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm and verify all factual claims before distribution. Fact verification remains essential and unchanged; provide supporting materials and ready documentation for reporters and aggregators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid boilerplate / meaningless superlatives
rubrics_metrics.description: AI summarization makes 'leading provider' boilerplate worthless
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't rely on generic self-descriptors (e.g., 'leading provider') or boilerplate company-speak; AI summarization and wire scrapers will strip or devalue these claims. Provide specific, verifiable details instead of fluff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience targeting: know who reads and who doesn't
rubrics_metrics.description: Target distribution to audiences that still read press releases and avoid wasting effort on those who don't
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Who still reads: wire scrapers (AI summarizers), trade press in regulated industries, local TV news producers, industry analysts, SEO tools/aggregators. Who doesn't: general business reporters at major outlets, podcast hosts, YouTube creators/influencers, social-native journalists, most consumer beat reporters. Use this to prioritize channels and tailor messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider replacing the press release with other owned channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Use founder X/Twitter thread, company Substack newsletter, LinkedIn carousel, podcast appearance, or investor letter instead of a traditional release when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For many announcements the most effective approach is to publish via founder/social channels or owned newsletters and pair with earned media (podcasts) rather than issuing a formal press release. Evaluate whether a release adds value or if owned/social channels will perform better.
